user.title: MXZ Coordinator
user.description:
Pick every indoor head connected to ONE MXZ outdoor unit (2–8). ORDER IS PRIORITY: the first head wins a heat-vs-cool standoff. Vane controls are detected automatically. For a second outdoor unit, add the integration again.

A head can only be claimed by one MXZ Coordinator at a time. While another setup or reconfigure dialog has a head selected, that head is reserved. The reservation is released when that dialog finishes, is cancelled, or is rejected at its last step. It has no timeout. Reconfiguring an entry can keep the heads that entry already owns, but not while another open dialog has one of them selected — finish that dialog first. If you cannot find it, restart Home Assistant.

data_description.demand_threshold: How far off target a room must be before the whole system may SWITCH between heating and cooling. Bigger = fewer mode changes. Most homes are fine with the default.
data_description.engage_deadband: After a room reaches its target it coasts with the fan. This is how far it may drift before conditioning kicks back in. Enter a value between 0.5–5 °F (0.25–2.5 °C).
data_description.mode_hysteresis: Minimum SECONDS between heating↔cooling switches — protects the compressor from rapid cycling. 600 = 10 minutes. Don't lower this unless you know why.
data_description.eco_cool_max: In away/eco mode the system stays off unless a room gets warmer than this. Think of it as vacation overheat protection.
data_description.eco_heat_min: In away/eco mode the system stays off unless a room gets colder than this. Vacation freeze protection.
data_description.clamp_min: The lowest setpoint your indoor units physically accept. Only change if your model's range differs — commands outside it get rejected by the unit.
data_description.clamp_max: The highest setpoint your indoor units physically accept.
data_description.resting_mode_bias: When no room needs anything, which mode should the system sit in? 'Last called' is right for most; pin cool or heat if your climate only ever needs one.
data_description.heat_lockout_floor: Even when heating is locked out for the season, a room colder than this still gets heat. A safety net, not a comfort setting.
data_description.cool_lockout_ceiling: Even when cooling is locked out for the season, a room hotter than this still gets cooling.
data_description.changeover_entity: Optional but recommended: pick your weather integration (or an outdoor temperature sensor) and the seasons handle themselves — heating locks out on warm days, cooling on cold ones. No weather entity? Add Home Assistant's built-in Met.no first.
data_description.changeover_heat_above: When the forecast daily high is at or above this, heating locks out (summer behavior).
data_description.changeover_cool_below: When the forecast daily high is at or below this, cooling locks out (winter behavior).
data_description.fan_boost_enable: Ramps the fan harder the further a room is from target, easing off as it arrives — like a car's auto climate. Recommended on.
data_description.fan_boost_max: The fastest fan speed the boost may use. Lower it if full blast is too loud for a bedroom.
data_description.inhibit_entity: Optional. Point this at a grid-status sensor, load-shed switch, or a 'vacation' boolean. While it's in the active state below, the coordinator parks its heads in a low-power hold and resumes normal coordination on its own when it clears — no automations needed. If this entity drops out (unavailable/unknown), the coordinator treats it as NOT held and keeps coordinating: a stuck sensor never parks the house.
data_description.inhibit_active_state: The state that means 'hold now' (default 'on'). Many grid sensors are inverted — they read 'off' when the grid is down — so set this to 'off' for those.
data_description.inhibit_action: How held heads sit during a hold. 'Eco' keeps freeze/overheat protection only (very low draw, recommended); 'Off' is zero draw with no protection; 'Fan only' just circulates air.
data_description.idle_action: 'Fan only' (default) keeps air moving while a room is satisfied. 'Off' stops the fan and the head closes its vanes — no airflow over the wet coil, which is what carries the after-cooling smell. The refrigerant valve behaves the same either way. 'Off after a coil-dry period' runs the fan briefly after cooling so the coil is not sealed wet, then turns the head off.
data_description.coil_dry_minutes: How long the fan runs after active cooling before the head turns off, so the coil dries instead of being sealed wet. Heating skips this — a heated coil is dry. Used only with 'Off after a coil-dry period'.

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure heads

Every head you keep takes its name, sensor, vane wiring, target, enable, drift and fan hold with it, wherever you move it in the list. Dropping a head deletes that room's entities. Name the rooms on the next step.

A head can only be claimed by one MXZ Coordinator at a time. While another setup or reconfigure dialog has a head selected, that head is reserved. The reservation is released when that dialog finishes, is cancelled, or is rejected at its last step. It has no timeout. Reconfiguring an entry can keep the heads that entry already owns, but not while another open dialog has one of them selected — finish that dialog first. If you cannot find it, restart Home Assistant.

init.title: MXZ Coordinator tuning
init.description: All temperatures use your Home Assistant unit (°C or °F). Idle action lists only modes every configured head supports; an incompatible stored choice must be changed explicitly and is never rewritten for you. Sensor freshness is optional, and its durations are minutes. An expected interval uses three missed reports as the maximum age; an explicit maximum age overrides that and must be at least one interval. Startup grace defaults to maximum age. Choose HA state write only when every write is a current acquisition. Sample timestamp needs exactly one trusted timestamp or sequence attribute. To remove a profile, clear its duration and marker fields before choosing Unknown.

shared_mode_legacy_option.title: Shared mode no longer offers "{stored}"
shared_mode_legacy_option.description:
Shared mode now offers only the two directions one outdoor unit can share: cool and heat. Arbitration resolved the stored "{stored}" to cool, so it was an unreliable stop control rather than a stop: with the coordinator running it could park a head that had been heating, and while the coordinator was disabled or held in a fixed-mode standby park it was simply retained on the selector. Shared mode now reads "{current}". The stored value does not say which direction the system had been running, nothing else changed, and no hold was created.

To stop the coordinator and leave the heads exactly where they are, turn off **Coordinator enable**. To hold the heads, use the standby hold entity (Configure → "Standby hold entity"): its default eco action still conditions a room that reaches the protection extremes, while its off or fan only action parks every head for as long as the hold lasts. To idle one room, turn off that room's enable switch. To stop a satisfied head's fan, set the idle action to "Off".

Dismiss this message once you have read it.
